figures.shows: Four-qubit QCNN: an encoding block, then Conv blocks on neighbouring qubit pairs, Pool blocks that halve the register, then a final Conv, Pool and a single-qubit measurement.

figures.shows: Four encodings on four qubits with inputs x0 to x3: (a) TPE, one RX(x_i) per qubit; (b) HEE, RX(x_i) layers followed by a CNOT chain, repeated Nlayer times; (c) CHE, Hadamards, RZ(x_i) and RZZ(x_i x_j) gates.

papers.what_it_is: A simulation study that compares small quantum convolutional neural networks (SO(4) and SU(4) blocks, four qubits) with parameter-matched classical CNNs for top-quark versus QCD jet-image classification, with a dimensional expressivity analysis that removes redundant circuit parameters.

assertions.value: The authors state that, to date, there is no established method to determine which type of data can be efficiently used in QML and how it must be embedded into a quantum circuit to surpass classical machine learning, and no systematic approach to constructing a QNN suited to a given problem.

assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement about the state of the field, without evidence in the paper.
